data.title: Single-Instance Deployment
data.tagline: Single-instance deployment keeps exactly one running replica of a service in its environment.
data.learningOutcome: You can identify which availability and in-memory-state risks concentrate in one instance and state how to verify them.
data.description: A background service with a replica count of 1 sends requests to one running instance. A release or crash restart can make it briefly unavailable, and in-memory work that was not written to durable storage may be lost. Single-instance deployment is not the Singleton pattern and does not mean data cannot be durable: it describes the number of runtime replicas, while a database or other durable store can exist separately.

learning.assumes: You know a service runs in an environment where it can be restarted or replaced.
learning.outcome: You can identify which availability and in-memory-state risks concentrate in one instance and state how to verify them.

explanation.title: The only replica defines the availability window
explanation.text: When one running instance handles the service, a release, crash, or maintenance event leaves no other replica of the same service to take over requests. Brief unavailability during restart is an expected risk; a successful deployment job does not mean users remain continuously connected.

explanation.title: Move required state out of process memory
explanation.text: Unfinished work in process memory may disappear when the instance stops, while records in durable storage can be read again after recovery. Verify service recovery, durable data, and which in-memory tasks may be lost separately. This improves recovery evidence but does not give one instance automatic failover.

explanation.title: An internal room-booking service can run as one instance
explanation.text: A low-traffic internal room-booking service can run as one instance for a simpler deployment. However, every booking entry point becomes briefly unavailable during a release, so choose an acceptable maintenance window and state this risk clearly.

data.boundary: Single-instance deployment describes the number of running replicas, not a Singleton code pattern. A single-instance service can still use a database and can later scale. Its key boundary is that only one service instance is available to receive requests, so restart and instance failure have no same-service replica ready to take over immediately.

lessonPractice.title: A single-instance service is restarting and users temporarily cannot open the page. Which judgment and verification are accurate?

options.label: Accept a brief restart outage and confirm durable data is readable after recovery
options.feedback: Correct. Availability risk is concentrated in the only replica, while data durability must be verified separately.

options.label: Delete the Singleton object in code to make deployment multi-instance and avoid the interruption
options.feedback: The Singleton pattern is a code structure; it cannot change runtime replica count or restart behavior.

options.label: Once the service is online again, assume every task kept in memory before restart still exists
options.feedback: Process memory normally disappears when the instance stops; recovery does not prove in-memory work was saved.

data.agentPrompt: Deploy this background service as a single instance and state the restart unavailability window when the replica count is 1. Check that task state is written to durable storage instead of keeping recoverable work only in process memory. Restart it once, confirm the service recovers and existing data is readable, and report the availability risk of the single instance.
